Plan around it or brief the provisioner. Centre Point Plaza, Ukunda junction · ~08:30–21:00 typical, unverified first-party

provisioning|Chandarana Foodplus.group: The cold chain — three supermarkets, three jobs
provisioning|Chandarana Foodplus.name: Chandarana Foodplus
provisioning|Chandarana Foodplus.teaser: Masalas, ghee, atta, dry mbaazi — the pantry for the coast's actual cooking.
provisioning|Chandarana Foodplus.body: The Kenyan family chain's south-coast outpost, strong on specialty, imported and Indian-Kenyan lines, wines and spirits. When the brief calls for cardamom, ghee or atta rather than French butter, this is the aisle — and the dry pigeon peas for a proper mbaazi live here too. Baharini Plaza, central strip · ~08:00–21:00 (directory-sourced) · +254 712 354 955

provisioning|Naivas, The Gate Mall.group: The cold chain — three supermarkets, three jobs
provisioning|Naivas, The Gate Mall.name: Naivas, The Gate Mall
provisioning|Naivas, The Gate Mall.teaser: Kenya's biggest homegrown chain — bulk staples where the locals shop.
provisioning|Naivas, The Gate Mall.body: A step cheaper than the beach-road pair, inland at the Gate Mall: dry staples, crates of water, cleaning, the unglamorous volume. Do bulk here, the cold chain on the strip, and the living produce at the market — three stops, three jobs. Aggregator hours conflict; call before an early run. Ukunda–Ramisi road · with the market in the same run

provisioning|Madafu · mnazi · mbata · ma.group: The coconut ladder — one tree, one economy
provisioning|Madafu · mnazi · mbata · ma.name: Madafu · mnazi · mbata · makuti
provisioning|Madafu · mnazi · mbata · ma.teaser: Drinking nut, palm wine, copra, thatch — most coastal farm households live off this one tree.
provisioning|Madafu · mnazi · mbata · ma.body: Madafu is the green drinking nut, opened roadside. Mnazi is the tapped palm wine — a morning product, drunk the same day. Mbata is the mature copra, graded milling (for oil) versus edible (chewed dry); the kitchens grate it on the mbuzi stool and press the cream by hand. Makuti thatch and coir rope use the rest. Chef's rule: madafu for guests, Kentaste for the pantry, mnazi only where it is tapped, before noon, where locals queue — and never serve it to guests untested. Everywhere in Kwale · the fruit calendar peaks with mangoes Nov–Mar (Ngowe Dec–Jan)

street-food|Kitchens close earlier than.group: The gap, and how to plan around it
street-food|Kitchens close earlier than.name: Kitchens close earlier than you think
street-food|Kitchens close earlier than.teaser: The Salty Squid's kitchen shuts at half eight. Always.
street-food|Kitchens close earlier than.body: Several beach kitchens here stop serving well before the evening feels finished — The Salty Squid 's closes at 20:30 without exception, and it is not the only one. If you are coming off a late dive, a sunset dhow or a long drive back from Shimoni, order by eight or accept that you are eating at a junction later. Eat early, or eat inland — those are the two options after nine on the beach road

street-food|Nothing moves before midnigh.group: The gap, and how to plan around it
street-food|Nothing moves before midnigh.name: Nothing moves before midnight
street-food|Nothing moves before midnigh.teaser: The night here starts after the food has stopped, not with it.
street-food|Nothing moves before midnigh.body: Diani's clubs — Shakatak , Full Moon , Tandoori , Manyatta — are empty before midnight and then everything at once. Shakatak's own description is exactly that. So the sequence that works is: eat properly by nine, drink somewhere on the sand until eleven, and go out after that. Trying to do it in the other order leaves you hungry. ⚠ Confirm any club on its own channel the same day. Several have a 2024 press trail from the streetlight-driven nightlife revival and a web presence that then goes cold — that gap is the caveat, not a detail. Weekend nights · cash and walk-in at most of them

street-food|The Ukunda junction, just af.name: The Ukunda junction, just after sunset
street-food|The Ukunda junction, just af.teaser: Where the boda riders and shop staff who run the strip eat — and it is cheap.
street-food|The Ukunda junction, just af.body: From late afternoon the junction fills with charcoal and karai pans: viazi karai in turmeric batter with chilli-tamarind, mishkaki over the coals, grilled corn at about twenty shillings. It sits at the town's transport heart, which is why it is still going when the beach road has gone quiet, and why the people eating there are the people who work here. KES 20 corn to low hundreds (obs. 2026-05) · walk up, point, pay cash or M-Pesa

street-food|Havana's late kitchen.name: Havana's late kitchen
street-food|Havana's late kitchen.teaser: The one strip address that will still feed you when the others have stopped.
street-food|Havana's late kitchen.body: Havana is the late plate on the beach road itself — the reason it appears on the Tuesday and Saturday lines of the week . If you are staying on the strip and do not want a taxi to a junction, this is the answer. Check the night before you rely on it; late service is the first thing to go in low season

street-food|Funky Monkey, to midnight.name: Funky Monkey, to midnight
street-food|Funky Monkey, to midnight.teaser: Bar food while the strip's one institutional party night runs.
street-food|Funky Monkey, to midnight.body: The bar runs to midnight Wednesday to Saturday , with the Hot Salsa night on Wednesdays — DJs, dancers, margarita flights. It bridges the gap between the kitchens closing and the clubs opening, which on this strip is a genuine service. WhatsApp a table for the Wednesday salsa night

landmarks|The Galu baobab.name: The Galu baobab
landmarks|The Galu baobab.teaser: The traditional end of Diani Beach is a tree.
landmarks|The Galu baobab.body: Diani's core runs from the Kongo river to Galu, and the traditional southern marker is an old baobab — a boundary drawn in botany rather than surveying. Baobabs punctuate the whole strip (the 41's bar is built around one; giants frame the mosque); they are protected in practice by reverence, which on this coast is older than law. Galu beach · the neighbouring kayas explain the reverence

landmarks|The colobridges.name: The colobridges
landmarks|The colobridges.teaser: Rope ladders over the traffic — community engineering you can watch working.
landmarks|The colobridges.body: Strung since 1997 over the nine-kilometre cut of 1971. Look up anywhere on the southern strip and eventually a troop crosses hand over hand above the matatus. The full story is in the green section ; the habit it should give you is a slow foot on the beach road. Diani Beach Road, densest toward the south

landmarks|Ukunda airstrip.name: Ukunda airstrip
landmarks|Ukunda airstrip.teaser: A 1,174 m tarmac runway between the beach and the highway — the coast's side door.
landmarks|Ukunda airstrip.body: KAA-owned, unofficially 'Diani Airport': Safarilink and Jambojet connect it daily (Jambojet: about an hour from Nairobi), which is why a Diani week no longer starts with the ferry. The skydivers' Caravans use it too — the beach landings you see are briefed in the water section . Diani Beach Road, Ukunda · arrival brief in the appendix

landmarks|The Two Fishes ruin.name: The Two Fishes ruin
landmarks|The Two Fishes ruin.teaser: One of the ten majors of the 80s, now a lived-in ruin — the strip's memento mori.
landmarks|The Two Fishes ruin.body: The Two Fishes hotel — German-founded, once among Diani's ten — did not survive the contraction; its shell is now inhabited and worked around by local families, notable enough as a condition to carry its own academic paper on 'the politics of skeletons and ruination'. It is not a sight to visit — people live there — but knowing it is there recalibrates every brochure superlative on the strip. Southern strip · respect: homes, not a photo stop

landmarks|Kongo Mosque.name: Kongo Mosque
landmarks|Kongo Mosque.teaser: Centuries of coral masonry, still praying — the strip's oldest working building.
landmarks|Kongo Mosque.body: The full brief is in Culture ; as a landmark it is the north end of everything — the estuary, the baobabs, the wade to Tiwi, the madafu trade, the sunset dugouts. Mwachema mouth, Diani north

landmarks|The Mteza bridge.name: The Mteza bridge
landmarks|The Mteza bridge.teaser: The longest bridge over water in Kenya — the reason your transfer no longer queues for a ferry.
landmarks|The Mteza bridge.body: The centrepiece of the Dongo Kundu bypass, opened August 2024, ending the Likoni ferry's monopoly on the south coast — a crossing that once moved over 300,000 people a day. Untolled at last dated report (Oct 2025); check before assuming. On the Mombasa approach · you will cross it without noticing, which is the point

landmarks|The Wasini pillar tomb.name: The Wasini pillar tomb
landmarks|The Wasini pillar tomb.teaser: Chinese porcelain set into a Swahili tomb — the Indian Ocean trade in one object.
landmarks|The Wasini pillar tomb.body: Wasini's old Wa-vumba settlement is built in and around its own ruins, and the pillar tomb still holding its inset Chinese porcelain says everything about what moved on the monsoon: goods, people, taste. Thirty seconds off the village path on the island hour. Wasini village · with the dhow day

landmarks|Sheldrick Falls.name: Sheldrick Falls
landmarks|Sheldrick Falls.teaser: The waterfall walk inside Shimba Hills — carry water, wear real shoes.
landmarks|Sheldrick Falls.body: The signed trailhead inside the reserve sends you down with a ranger to the falls — the green hour of the Shimba day between the sable glades and the viewpoints. Brief in the green section . Shimba Hills · mornings, before the heat climbs the hill

craft|★ Diving the Crab.name: ★ Diving the Crab
craft|★ Diving the Crab.teaser: A PADI 5★ IDC resort: the tier that certifies instructors, not just divers.
craft|★ Diving the Crab.body: Why this one. The coast's senior dive operation has worked this reef since 1985, and it is a PADI 5 Star IDC Resort — the level that trains new instructors, not merely new divers. That means you can start here never having breathed underwater and, if you keep coming back, end up qualified to teach it, on the same reef the whole way. Own pool, Nitrox, six instructors, around twenty-nine sites within a forty-minute boat ride. And it has been here long enough to change the seabed: it created the coast's signature wreck by re-sinking the MV Alpha Funguo as an artificial reef. Based at the Nomad beach · book the course, not a single dive, if you want the ladder divingthecrab.com →

craft|H2O Extreme.group: The others, and what each is missing
craft|H2O Extreme.name: H2O Extreme
craft|H2O Extreme.teaser: Kiting here since 2003, IKO-certified — and it moved beach to teach on better water.
craft|H2O Extreme.body: Two decades on this water and IKO-affiliated, so the certificate is a real one. It moved from central Diani to Galu for a reason it states plainly: clearer water, wider beach, better riding away from the mid-strip tides and boat traffic. A school that relocates to improve its teaching water is taking the teaching seriously. Missing: no instructor is named publicly — a reputable room, but you do not know whose hands you are in until you arrive. Its wind page defines the two seasons properly — kaskazi N/NE mid-Dec to mid-March, kusi the rest h2o-extreme.com →

craft|Kite254.group: The others, and what each is missing
craft|Kite254.name: Kite254
craft|Kite254.teaser: Radio-helmet coaching in a waist-deep lagoon — you hear the fix mid-mistake.
craft|Kite254.body: Two bases , current Ozone kites, and radio-helmet instruction so the coaching arrives while you are still making the error rather than afterwards on the beach. The waist-deep, reef-protected lagoon is the pedagogy: you can stand up and start again. Roughly six months of trade wind a year. Missing: same as above — no named instructor published. Bases at Pallet Cafe on southern Galu and at Diani Sea Lodge kite254.com →

craft|Akamba Handicraft Co-operative.group: The others, and what each is missing
craft|Akamba Handicraft Co-operative.name: Akamba Handicraft Co-operative
craft|Akamba Handicraft Co-operative.teaser: Since 1963, ~2,800 carvers, and 70–80% of each sale goes to the maker.
craft|Akamba Handicraft Co-operative.body: Founded in 1963 by around a hundred Kamba carvers who brought the Wamunyu tradition to Mombasa, now roughly 2,800 members working rosewood, ebony and neem by hand. You walk the open sheds and watch a piece go from log selection through rough carving, detailing and finishing — and buy from the co-op store, where seventy to eighty per cent goes to the carver , against a fraction of that on the beach. Missing: no classes. You can watch and buy, and you can meet the individual carvers, but you cannot join. Buy here rather than on the sand — and see the warning below on what “ebony” usually is akambahandicraftcoop.com →

craft|Diani Art Club.group: The others, and what each is missing
craft|Diani Art Club.name: Diani Art Club
craft|Diani Art Club.tag: missing: it's a gallery, not a school
craft|Diani Art Club.teaser: Jimmy, the resident portrait painter — the one named practising maker on this list.
craft|Diani Art Club.body: A working gallery on the Ukunda–Diani road dedicated to Kenyan artists, from bold abstracts to Maasai handcraft, with resident portrait painter Jimmy taking commissions — and real, seasonally published opening hours, which on this strip is itself a mark of seriousness. Missing: commissions, not classes. If you want something made by a named person you can meet, this is it; if you want to learn to make it, this is not. It also sells safari bookings, which tells you its scale honestly diani-artclub.com →

craft|Kaya Kinondo.group: The others, and what each is missing
craft|Kaya Kinondo.name: Kaya Kinondo
craft|Kaya Kinondo.tag: missing: nothing — it is not a school
craft|Kaya Kinondo.teaser: A community deciding, on its own terms, what outsiders may see.
craft|Kaya Kinondo.body: Thirty hectares of coral-rag forest sacred to the Digo, an inscribed component of the UNESCO Sacred Mijikenda Kaya Forests and a national monument since 1992. In 2001 the elders made a sacrifice to the ancestors and opened it under controlled terms. Here because the thing being practised — a community governing access to its own sacred ground — is the most intact living tradition on this coast, and the model the Wasini and Gazi boardwalks follow. It is a guided visit on the community's terms, and that is not a shortcoming; it is the point. Go with the community guide, cover up, and do not photograph what you are asked not to kayakinondotrails.com →

craft|The Kaaribu street-food walk.group: The nearest thing to enrolment, and the honest warning
craft|The Kaaribu street-food walk.name: The Kaaribu street-food walk
craft|The Kaaribu street-food walk.teaser: A registered company, a fixed route, and the door into rooms you would not enter alone.
craft|The Kaaribu street-food walk.body: Ninety minutes with Kaaribu Experiences, a registered Kenyan company: meet at Tsunami Garden Cafe, walk the Ibiza market trading cluster, eat in a kibandaski — cardamom-coconut porridge, viazi karai, chapati and beans, ugali na sukuma, coconut rice with fish — and finish with an mnazi tasting. It is the honest way into the mangwe , which is not a walk-in. Bookable as an outsider · the market and the palm-wine dens both come with it kaaribu.com →

craft|What is sold as craft and is not.group: The nearest thing to enrolment, and the honest warning
craft|What is sold as craft and is not.name: What is sold as craft and is not
craft|What is sold as craft and is not.teaser: Most of the “ebony” on this beach is lighter wood under shoe polish.
craft|What is sold as craft and is not.body: Real mpingo is heavy and dark all the way through; scratch an unseen face and see whether the colour survives. Most stall “ebony” on the strip does not. Buy at the Akamba co-op sheds instead, where the carver keeps seventy to eighty per cent, and expect to pay more for a piece that is what it says it is. The same applies to the story: do not believe a line about a grandfather unless you are watching the grandfather. Bargaining is expected on the beach; it is not expected at the co-op or from a named artist

hot-foot|The humpbacks are through.name: The humpbacks are through
hot-foot|The humpbacks are through.teaser: The operators' whale window is open now, and closes with September.
hot-foot|The humpbacks are through.body: Humpbacks run up the East African coast from the start of August to about mid-October, and the Diani operators run their dedicated whale expeditions from 15 August to the end of September . That is the window, and it is short. Book it as a search rather than a sighting. Whale Shark Adventures works two microlight spotter aircraft, which covers far more water than a boat alone; Ocean Tribe runs trips too. Peak season start of August to mid-October; the operator window is 15 Aug–30 Sep

hot-foot|⚠ The whale sharks are NOT in.name: ⚠ The whale sharks are NOT in
hot-foot|⚠ The whale sharks are NOT in.teaser: The thing this coast is named for is four months away. Do not be sold it now.
hot-foot|⚠ The whale sharks are NOT in.body: Whale-shark season on this coast runs October to March, peaking in January and February . In late August they are not here. Operators start seeing the first arrivals at the beginning of October, and there are trips where humpbacks and whale sharks have been seen on the same day — but that is October onwards, not now. This is the single most mis-sold thing in Diani. If somebody offers you a whale-shark trip in August, they are offering you a boat ride. ⚠ Book whale sharks for Jan–Feb if that is what you came for

hot-foot|The kusi is feeding the fishery.name: The kusi is feeding the fishery
hot-foot|The kusi is feeding the fishery.teaser: Cooler, rougher, and the best pelagic action of the year.
hot-foot|The kusi is feeding the fishery.body: The south-easterly is blowing: breezier air, showers rolling through roughly two or three days a week, and cooler, rougher water. The seas are more sporting and the diving is less glassy than kaskazi — but the nutrient-rich water balls the baitfish, and this is prime time for yellowfin tuna and giant trevally . Deep-sea fishing is excellent along the whole Kenyan coast from September to March, so it is just coming on. The same wind is why the dawn auction at Mwaepe is worth the early alarm this month. Kusi runs roughly June to September · expect a wetter crossing to Wasini

hot-foot|A deep partial lunar eclipse, 2.name: A deep partial lunar eclipse, 27–28 August
hot-foot|A deep partial lunar eclipse, 2.teaser: Africa is inside the visibility zone.
hot-foot|A deep partial lunar eclipse, 2.body: On the night of 27–28 August 2026 the Earth's umbral shadow covers roughly 96 per cent of the Moon — a partial eclipse only on a technicality. The umbral phase runs 01:23 to 07:01 UTC, which is 04:23 to 10:01 East Africa Time , greatest around 07:12 EAT. Africa is in the visibility zone. The catch here is the same as anywhere on this longitude: the Moon sets around dawn, so the watchable part is the pre-dawn umbral phase. Check a local ephemeris on the day — we have not verified Diani's moonset time. ⚠ Published UTC window converted to EAT (UTC+3). Confirm local moonset before setting an alarm.

hot-foot|Spring tides around the 28th.name: Spring tides around the 28th
hot-foot|Spring tides around the 28th.teaser: The widest low water of the month — reef walks on, and the fishery lands more.
hot-foot|Spring tides around the 28th.body: The moon outranks the weekday on this coast. A full moon on 28 August means the spring tides either side give the lowest lows of the month: the lagoon inside the reef empties far enough to walk, the sandbanks come up, and the landings are at their biggest. Plan the reef walk and the dawn fish run for those days, and read the tide table before you commit any morning. Reef walks documented from Tiwi still start from Twiga Lodge

hot-foot|⚠ Mango is not in season.name: ⚠ Mango is not in season
hot-foot|⚠ Mango is not in season.teaser: The coast's main crop is three months away, whatever the menu says.
hot-foot|⚠ Mango is not in season.body: Coast Province is Kenya's main mango region and its first and main season runs November to February . Late August is not it. Mango is available year-round and it is not at its best now — so a "seasonal mango" special in August is selling you the calendar rather than the fruit. Buy at the Mvindeni market and ask what actually came in this week instead. Market prices, cash or M-Pesa · morning of a market day

hot-foot|Tuna and trevally at the landin.name: Tuna and trevally at the landings
hot-foot|Tuna and trevally at the landin.teaser: The cooler water is putting bigger pelagics within reach of the small boats.
hot-foot|Tuna and trevally at the landin.body: The nutrient-rich kusi water is the reason to buy fish this month rather than last. Shimoni lands the tuna-and-kingfish class the Diani reef does not; Mwaepe is the one you can walk to from the Galu hotels. Both are finished by mid-morning — negotiate on the sand, cash, and ask for the BMU chairman if you are buying quantity. 06:00–09:00 at Mwaepe · combine Shimoni with a Wasini crossing

hot-foot|The Diani Film Festival has jus.name: The Diani Film Festival has just been
hot-foot|The Diani Film Festival has jus.teaser: Its second edition ran at Nyali Cinemax and is over for this year.
hot-foot|The Diani Film Festival has jus.body: The Diani Film Festival's second edition ran on 31 July and 1 August 2026 at Nyali Cinemax. It was started to address the shortage of cinemas in Kenya and particularly in Diani, and to give Kenyan filmmaking a room to argue in. If you care, note it for next year rather than looking for it now. Second edition, 2026 · Nyali Cinemax

hot-foot|Nothing major in September — sa.name: Nothing major in September — said plainly
hot-foot|Nothing major in September — sa.teaser: We found no significant Diani or Kwale festival for September 2026.
hot-foot|Nothing major in September — sa.body: We looked and did not find one. There are scattered listings on the national event platforms for September dates, but nothing on the scale of the film festival or the kite festival that would justify planning a trip around it, and nothing we could verify well enough to print. That is not a gap in the coast, it is the shape of its year: this is the tail of the kusi, the quiet end of the low season before the whale sharks and the December crowd. You are here for the fishing, the empty sand and the prices. ⚠ Absence of evidence, honestly labelled — check the local listings if a date matters to you
